children: fell 12.40% premarket after the Swiss drugmaker said del-desiran failed its Phase III HARBOR study in myotonic dystrophy type 1, showing no statistically significant improvement over placebo on hand opening time. It's the third setback in a week. Pelacarsen missed on cardiovascular risk reduction days earlier, and eight trials of the cell therapy rap-cel were paused after three patients died.

Del-desiran came with Avidity Biosciences, which Novartis bought for around $12 billion last year, and is one of three antibody oligonucleotide conjugate therapies added to its neuromuscular pipeline in that deal. Barclays called it the test case for the deal and put del-desiran and pelacarsen together at roughly $5 billion in risk-adjusted peak sales. The firm expects the shares to materially underperform and said the company's "20% sector premium may now be debated."

Novartis reiterated its 5% to 6% average annual sales growth target through 2030. Jefferies said the goal will likely be seen as unattainable without further M&A, and noted that management's ability to do large deals is now itself under scrutiny.

title: Novartis Stock Falls 12% on Its Third Trial Setback In a Week
